newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia chemical industry profits fall 18 pct.
newsitem.headline: Australia chemical industry profits fall 18 pct.

text.p: Profits generated by Australia's chemicals and plastics industry fell 18 percent to A$262 million in calendar 1996, the Plastics and Chemicals Industry Association (PACIA) said on Wednesday.
"1996 was a tough year for the chemical industry in Australia", said John Foote, PACIA president and chairman and managing director of DuPont Australia and New Zealand.
Total sales including exports fell four percent to A$5.58 billion, producing a general return on investment of five percent, Foote said in a statement.
A PACIA report also said the industry could invest as much as A$6 billion in new projects should the investment climate in Australia improve, Foote said.
"We have a window of opportunity of about two years and if the government should introduce more competitive investment and tax policies, those projects could well go ahead,", said Foote.
Employment in the chemical industry fell one percent to 10,555 people, but further significant cuts were unlikely in 1997, Foote said.

Research and development expenditure fell 13 percent in 1996 and this decline would probably continue because of the government's decision to cut R&D tax concessions to 125 percent from 150 percent, he said.
Australia's other major major chemicals companies include ICI Australia Ltd and units of Wesfarmers Ltd and Gibson Chemical Industries Ltd.
